subject.title: [Feature] Decouple dreaming from memory-core — allow any memory plugin to implement dreaming protocol

question: Should OpenClaw add a public plugin-SDK dreaming provider protocol, or keep non-memory-core dreaming as plugin-owned standalone orchestration through ClawHub?
rationale: Current main has a memory-core dreaming sidecar workaround, while the requested protocol would add durable public SDK/config/runtime surface and should align with the open memory role-slot architecture work.

options.title: Design a public dreaming protocol
options.body: Define the plugin SDK/config/scheduler contract so memory plugins can implement dreaming storage and lifecycle behavior under OpenClaw-managed orchestration.

options.title: Wait for role-slot architecture
options.body: Keep this issue open until the broader memory role-slot PR lands or closes, then design dreaming on top of that settled taxonomy.

options.title: Keep dreaming plugin-owned
options.body: Document ClawHub standalone dreaming plugins as the supported path and close the core protocol request after maintainer approval.

recommendation.title: Design a public dreaming protocol
recommendation.body: Define the plugin SDK/config/scheduler contract so memory plugins can implement dreaming storage and lifecycle behavior under OpenClaw-managed orchestration.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest recent cross-cutting memory/plugin/SDK history in the inspected files and is therefore the best available owner for the product-boundary decision.
